History:
• 2-day history of constant, gradually worsening burning pain localized just below the umbilicus; tender to palpation per patient.  
• Associated symptoms: subjective feeling of being “hot and sweaty,” mild nausea (no vomiting).  
• Urinary: increased frequency; urine noted to be “pink” in color. Denies dysuria or suprapubic burning.  
• Bowel: brief constipation last week, now resolved; no diarrhea.  
• No shortness of breath, cough, palpitations, headache, or visual disturbance.  
• Sexually active with one partner; last intercourse 4 days ago. On etonogestrel implant (Implanon) placed 1 year ago. Last menstrual period reported as “about three weeks ago…maybe two weeks ago” (conflict noted). No prior similar abdominal pain episodes.

Past Medical History:
• Chronic illnesses: none reported.  
• Surgical history: none.  
• Allergies: not documented.  
• Current medications: etonogestrel implant (Implanon); no other regular drugs.  
• Social: non-smoker; social alcohol use; accountant; lives with two roommates.

Physical Examination:
(Note: findings based on patient report—no in-office exam performed)  
• General: alert; feels hot/sweaty (temperature not measured).  
• Abdomen: patient-reported localized tenderness below umbilicus.  
• Genitourinary: no reported flank pain; no dysuria.  
• Cardiopulmonary: denies dyspnea, cough, palpitations.  
• Neurologic: no headaches or visual changes.

Impression:
Lower abdominal pain with possible urinary tract infection; pregnancy and other intra-abdominal causes not yet excluded.

Management Plan:
• Empiric antibiotic: Trimethoprim, 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days (dose/route/frequency per transcript; specific mg not documented).  
• Advise home pregnancy test to rule out pregnancy.  
• Symptomatic care: acetaminophen (paracetamol) for pain; maintain adequate oral hydration; consider cranberry juice.  
• Safety-net: return or call sooner if pain worsens, develops fever, vomiting, or other concerning symptoms.  
• Follow-up: re-evaluation in a few days if no improvement.

Patient Summary:
Patient with 2-day history of progressive lower abdominal pain, pink urine, and mild constitutional symptoms. Empiric treatment for presumed UTI started while arranging pregnancy exclusion. Patient instructed on red-flag symptoms and follow-up.

Key Takeaways:
1. Start Trimethoprim today and complete the 3-day course.  
2. Perform a home pregnancy test as soon as possible.  
3. Seek medical attention if pain intensifies, fever develops, or no improvement within several days.

Next Steps:
• Pregnancy test result to be communicated to provider.  
• If symptoms persist or worsen, consider urine analysis/culture, abdominal exam, and additional imaging or labs.  
• Schedule follow-up appointment if needed after antibiotic course.
